initial.title: Enhanced Visual Clarity of Attachment
initial.objective: Improve the visibility of the intended attachment surface and the actual attachment point to enhance viewer understanding.

interventions.rationale: By staging the cabinet behind or beside Mimi's finger, viewers can clearly see the intended attachment surface and the actual attachment point, enhancing the comedic effect of the failed attempt.

choreography.instruction: Mimi reaches toward the toy cabinet with a sticky note; the note visibly clings to her finger instead of sticking to the cabinet.
choreography.consequencePresentation: The note sticks to Mimi's finger, not the cabinet.

production.cameraComposition: Close-up on Mimi's hand showing the sticky note clinging to her finger, with the cabinet clearly visible in the background.

spatialRelationships.instruction: Mimi reaches toward the cabinet with a sticky note, her finger visibly sticking to the note.

production.temporalPresentation: 0-2s: Mimi reaches toward the toy cabinet with a sticky note; the note visibly clings to her finger instead of sticking to the cabinet.

initial.title: Separated Action and Result Visibility
initial.objective: Enhance the clarity of Mimi's action and the resulting state of the sticky notes.

interventions.rationale: By separating the action of peeling the note and the result of it splitting into two, viewers can better understand the transition and the resulting chaos of the sticky notes.

choreography.instruction: Mimi tries to peel the stuck note away with her other hand; the note splits into two.
choreography.consequencePresentation: One note sticks to each hand.

production.cameraComposition: Medium shot showing Mimi struggling to peel the note, with the two resulting notes clearly visible in each hand.

spatialRelationships.instruction: Mimi tries to peel the sticky note away with her other hand.
The note splits into two, with one note sticking to each hand.

production.temporalPresentation: 2-5s: Mimi tries to peel the stuck note away with her other hand; the note splits into two, with one note sticking to each hand.
